intro.text: Hi, thanks for having me. I'm Jane. I've been working as a DevOps engineer for almost six years, mostly on AWS and Kubernetes, and for the last three years I've led the platform team at Acme.

kubernetes_strong.text: Sure. We ran Amazon EKS with three managed node groups spread across three availability zones. Karpenter handled node autoscaling and the horizontal pod autoscaler scaled deployments on CPU and request rate. Ingress went through an application load balancer, and we used pod disruption budgets and topology spread constraints so losing a zone never took a service down. Prometheus and Grafana covered monitoring, and Argo CD did the deployments.

cost_vague.text: We reduced cloud costs by forty percent, mostly by rightsizing.

cost_specific.text: Monthly spend went from about one hundred and twenty thousand dollars to roughly seventy thousand over six months. The biggest single win was moving our batch processing to spot instances, then rightsizing the RDS databases and adding savings plans for the steady baseline. We tracked it weekly with Cost Explorer and tagged every resource by team.

dont_know.text: Hmm, I'm honestly not sure about that one. I haven't worked with it directly.

generic_medium.text: In my last role I approached that by first collecting metrics to understand the real bottleneck, then I wrote a short design proposal, reviewed it with the team, and rolled the change out gradually behind a feature flag so we could roll back quickly if something went wrong.

incident.text: The worst incident I handled was a certificate expiry that took down our public API for about twenty minutes. I coordinated the response, rotated the certificate, and afterwards we added automated expiry alerts thirty days ahead and moved certificates to cert manager so renewal became automatic.

coding_think_aloud.text: Okay, I'll go through the array once and keep a hash map from each value to its index. For every number I check whether the complement, target minus the number, is already in the map. That makes it linear time with linear extra space.

complexity.text: The time complexity is O of n because each element is visited once, and the space complexity is also O of n for the hash map in the worst case. With an empty input it just returns an empty result.

no_questions.text: No, I think you covered everything. Thank you very much for your time.
